Q: Why do my results different following along the tiny asm example? A:

I reached the same size removing the same two types of bloat: alignment padding and metadata.

nasm -f elf32 tiny.asm
gcc -m32 -s -no-pie -nostdlib -Wl,-N -Wl,--build-id=none tiny.o -o tiny_peter32
/usr/bin/x86_64-linux-gnu-ld.bfd: warning: tiny_peter32 has a LOAD segment with RWX permissions

Obtained size:
-rwxrwxr-x 1 peter john 248 May 4 00:01 tiny_peter32
-rwxrwxr-x 1 peter john 248 May 4 00:00 tiny_cordes32 (main/first OP answer replication, equivalent to: “a.out” from “foo.asm”)

Alignment / Alignment+Permissions: 
-Wl,-N (OMAGIC) is more aggressive. it disables the 4KB page alignment and makes the code section writable. (-Wl,--nmagic (NMAGIC) disables alignment but keeps the code read-only).
-s prevents the linker from writing symbol tables (equivalent to post command-line strip).
--build-id=none removes the .note.gnu.build-id section.


I tried many options that were about to work, but I was getting all the time the same error: /usr/bin/x86_64-linux-gnu-ld.bfd: tiny_peter32: error: PHDR segment not covered by LOAD segment /usr/bin/x86_64-linux-gnu-ld.bfd: warning: tiny_peter32 has a LOAD segment with RWX permissions collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status

All changed when adding -no-pie that removes the structures required for that kind of executable.

Q: How to force a transparent status bar on Samsung in Kotlin Multiplatform A:

write after the theme SongBookTheme and the background of the page will become the background of the line

ViewCompat.setOnApplyWindowInsetsListener(R.id.main) { view, insets ->
    val systemBars = insets.getInsets(WindowInsetsCompat.Type.systemBars())
    view.setPadding(systemBars.left, systemBars.top, systemBars.right, systemBars.bottom)
    insets
}

Q: Venn diagrams with heatmap A:

You can use the venn-diagram-lab library. It allows you to create Venn diagrams for multiple sets and easily customize the shading/colors based on values, which effectively solves the heatmap visualization for sets.

First, install it:

Bash

pip install venn-diagram-lab

Then you can use it like this to create a colored Venn diagram:

Python

from venn_diagram_lab import Dataset, analyze

  data = {
      "Set A": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5],
      "Set B": [4, 5, 6, 7, 8],
      "Set C": [1, 4, 8, 9, 10],
  }

  ds = Dataset.from_dict(data)            # accepts sets or lists; coerces to str
  result = analyze(ds)                    # picks a 3-set model automatically

  # Per-set custom colors (A, B, C…I), hex strings:
  svg = result.render_venn(colors={
      "A": "#440154",   # viridis-ish purple
      "B": "#21918c",   # teal
      "C": "#fde725",   # yellow
  })
  svg.save("venn.svg")
  # also: svg.save("venn.png") — needs cairo (brew install cairo on macOS)

Disclosure: I am the creator of this library. I built it to simplify this specific visualization task and provide more flexibility than the standard alternatives.

Q: How can I make Bash expand wildcards in variables? A:

You can write a function:

function expand { for arg in "$@"; do [[ -f $arg ]] && echo $arg; done }

then call it with what you want to expand:

expand "$MYDIR/"*.$SUFFIXES

You can also make it a script expand.sh if you like.

Q: /proc/kcore file is huge A:

You need to clean up files that are deleted but reserved:

tune2fs -m 1 /dev/<drive>

This should free reserved block space and give access to the privileged processes' reserved disk space. 1 is the percentage that will be allocated to the privileged processes afterwards. Do this only if you have enough disk space for critical processes like syslog and ssh.

You will never gain disk space by removing files from '/proc'. It is a virtual filesystem that has nothing to do with space on your HDD.

Q: flutter 3.3 ShaderCompilerException ink_sparkle.frag failed with exit code -1073740791 A:

I was getting same error while running unit tests, and the first test of the file was failing with this exception.

Simple fix, which worked for me is to run below commands in the order

flutter clean
flutter pub get
flutter run

And thats it, all restored well.

Q: How to use substitution in xargs? A:

Since curly braces as notation raises the concern of interpretation as metachar as opposed to a literal, I usually give a string to -I that is unlikely to appear in the input. Note that what I write below won't give you a swapped extension, but maybe the expression in the OP can be cast to do so, or a second pass does fixup.

find . -type f -name "*.txt" | xargs -IFNORD cp FNORD FNORD.dat

Q: `PostAsJsonAsync` returns 500 Internal Server Error from Azure Functions while Postman and `PostAsync` with `StringContent` succeed A:

PostAsJsonAsync is really an extension method that uses JsonContent instead of StringContent. Problem might be that it's using chunked encoding.

More info in this this github issue which should be describing your exact problem:

Refer to #49357

As the issue #49357 been closed due to this comment:

Given there is no detail about wide-spread server usage with chunked encoding disabled / not working, we should close this until

more evidence appears.

I have to say the Azure Logic App HTTP trigger doesn't support "chunked encoding". In Handle large messages with chunking in Azure Logic Apps doc, it says:

Logic App triggers don't support chunking because of the increased overhead of exchanging multiple messages.
